page: Vultr voc-s-8c-64gb-1280s-amd is an instance in the Optimized Cloud Compute family configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical AMD EPYC processor cores running at 2.0 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture with multithreading enabled at two threads per core, the system includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a high 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, paired with 1280 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage and one complimentary public IPv4 address. The configuration does not feature dedicated GPU acceleration.

Benchmark results show strong single-thread execution and robust memory subsystems. The instance scored 2933.77 in stress-ng single-core tests and 2766.09 in the PassMark memory evaluation, both landing in the upper quartile of evaluated machines. Standard multi-core metrics remain balanced across the middle tier, yielding a multi-core Geekbench score of 8979.0 and a multi-threaded stress-ng score of 23239.79. Large-block memory transfers achieve 127.29 GB/sec read and 75.3 GB/sec write bandwidth, supporting 15.7 million Redis SET operations per second. However, CPU-based machine learning inference is restricted, registering an average 14.38 tokens per second on 7B parameter text generation and lower-quartile prompt evaluation throughput.

The 1:8 compute-to-memory ratio coupled with direct-attached NVMe storage delivers high operational efficiency for memory-heavy and disk-intensive deployments without requiring external volume attachment overhead. Due to its dedicated core allocation and elevated memory density, the server is well matched for relational databases, in-memory datastores, CI/CD compilation pipelines, and transactional web application servers.
description: Vultr voc-s-8c-64gb-1280s-amd is a memory-dense compute instance within the Optimized Cloud Compute family. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical AMD EPYC cores operating at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The server is configured with 64.0 GB of system memory, a 1280 GB local NVMe solid-state drive, and one public IPv4 address, operating without discrete GPU accelerators. Benchmarks highlight strong single-core CPU throughput and top-tier memory benchmark scores, supported by 127.29 GB/sec uncached memory read bandwidth and 15.7 million Redis operations per second. Multi-core compute performance remains steady within median percentiles, while small-model LLM generation maintains workable throughput. The substantial RAM allocation per core alongside integrated fast storage makes this system well suited for database management systems, in-memory caches, software compilation, and backend application hosting.
